We need to decide for each column whether its value would already exist and be final at prediction time: prediction is made from the 1990 census and 1990 LEMAS survey, before the 1995 crime figures are published. So any data that is from 1990 census or 1990 LEMAS survey is available. Anything that depends on crime figures from 1995 (or later) is unavailable. Also any column that is derived from crime data (like assaultPerPop, burglPerPop, etc.) would be unavailable because they are crime statistics from 1995? Actually the target is violentPerPop (violent crimes per population) predicted from 1990 census and 1990 LEMAS before 1995 crime figures are published. So the dataset likely includes both predictor variables (census, LEMAS) and outcome variables (crime rates from 1995). The columns list includes many variables: some are demographic, some are police-related, some are crime counts (assaults, burglaries, murders, rapes, larcenies, autoTheft, arsons, robberies, etc.) and per population versions. Those crime-related columns would be unavailable at prediction time because they are the outcome (or related) from 1995. However some police-related variables like policePerPop, policeFieldPerPop, numPolice, policCallPerPop, etc., might be from 1990 LEMAS survey (law enforcement management and administrative stats) thus available. Need to infer which columns are from census vs LEMAS vs crime.

Given the dataset name "CRIME" likely from UCI Communities and Crime dataset. In that dataset, the prediction target is violent crimes per population (ViolentCrimesPerPop). The predictors include demographic, socioeconomic, housing, education, employment, etc., plus some law enforcement variables (like police per population, etc.) from 1990 LEMAS. The crime variables (like assaults, burglaries, etc.) are also from 1995 FBI UCR? Actually the dataset includes both 1990 census and 1990 LEMAS as predictors, and the 1995 crime data as target. Some columns are crime statistics (like murders, rapes, robberies, assaults, burglaries, larcenies, autoTheft, arsons) and also per population versions. Those are not available at prediction time because they are part of the outcome (or related) from 1995. However some columns like "assaultPerPop" might be a predictor? Actually assaultPerPop is likely a crime rate from 1995, thus unavailable. Similarly "burglPerPop", "larcPerPop", "autoTheftPerPop", "arsonsPerPop", "rapesPerPop", "murdPerPop", "nonViolPerPop", "robbbPerPop" etc. Also "violentPerPop" is target.

Thus we need to label each column as AVAILABLE if it's from 1990 census or 1990 LEMAS; UNAVAILABLE if it's from 1995 crime data; ABSTAIN if uncertain.
